mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where INDPRO falls for four straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their previous 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed their 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between HOUST (housing starts) and GDPC1 over a six-month window signals robust residential investment and broad demand strength, which supports earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Pearson correlation(HOUST, GDPC1) > 0.7 over six months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.10) when HOUST and GDPC1 are strongly positively correlated over six months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (payroll employment) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market and wage inflation, which pressures profit margins but also indicates economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of three consecutive months with monthly PAYEMS growth above 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in RSAFS (retail sales) for five consecutive months signals weakening consumer spending, which reduces revenue for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of strong monetary easing.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for five consecutive months and FEDFUNDS is not falling (FEDFUNDS change <= 0%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where RSAFS declines for five months and FEDFUNDS is not falling.
